comment: A buck or two more doesn't bother me, the music is still why I pay. What is driving me up the wall is the home screen shoving podcasts at me and making me hunt through three menus just to get to my music. Fix that and I'm happy.

Another price hike and artists still get fractions of a cent per stream. They can raise it to $20 for all I care, the money is going to the label and the executives, not the people who make the music. I already moved over for that reason, the only thing keeping me here now is habit.

$1 more and still no lossless. Tidal already gives me CD quality for less, and I only stay on Spotify for Connect and Discover Weekly. Raising the price while the hi-fi tier is still a promise is pretty rough.

Okay, so they want more money for the same enhance feature that keeps dumping recommended songs into my playlists. I already cancelled over that stuff so I'm not really the target here. Still annoyed though.

I'm on free so this doesn't hit me directly. Still, every price bump makes Premium harder to justify when I can't even pick my own songs without paying. Ads and shuffle-only is the reason I'd pay, not the price.

Cool, now it costs more and still doesn't have lossless or Spatial Audio. Apple Music is already at that price with better sound, and the Spotify UI keeps getting more cluttered. I'm going to be switching back to Apple Music for good.
A buck extra for something I use every single day is still a steal. Premium is still one of the best subscriptions I pay for. My only real gripe is ads creeping in more and more over time.

Raising the price while the home screen looks like absolute TikTok garbage?? Are you kidding me. Fix the home screen or I'm cancelling my membership and going to Tidal, I'm not paying more for huge blocks of suggestions.
Honestly a dollar is fine if they bring back album-based radio. Price is not the issue for me, it's the features getting stripped out. Still the most feature-rich thing I've tried.
Family went from $15.99 to $16.99. Split between the people in my house that's pretty much nothing, so the plan is still worth it. Hoping the plan switching doesn't turn into a billing mess though.

still the same awful layout, the music tab is a dumb card style instead of album tiles and now they want MORE money for it?? I already canceled over this. If they turn the album view back I'd pay again but right now I'm switching to Apple Music.
I already cancelled and the renewal pop up still appears every single time I open the app. Gets in the way when I'm trying to pause or skip. Cleared the cache, reinstalled, nothing. Driving me nuts.

So they want more money for ad-free music, but the podcast ads still play for Premium users and the podcast push is still everywhere. Gotta make money somehow my ass. I'm getting really close to just going to YouTube Premium.
A dollar more for something I literally can't live without. I've been on Premium for years and I'm not leaving. Just wish the cancel and renewal flow didn't keep nagging me.

Great, more money for a shuffle that still plays the same top 20 songs over and over. I love Spotify Connect and the rest of the app but I'm getting real tired of this. Pandora or Apple Music starts looking pretty good.
Honestly, still worth it. Free is too restricted to be useful and I'd keep Premium even if I cut everything else. The UI changes and pop-up suggestions are what I'm annoyed about, not a dollar.
A dollar more and it's still worth every penny. Unlimited skips, no ads, offline mode, I use it every day. Not going anywhere.

Raising the price while the liked-song hearts are still missing from album lists? No thanks. I already unsubscribed once over the liked songs changes and I'll do it again if the hearts don't come back. Apple Music is sitting right there.

Still no lossless for a buck more. 320 is fine for my AirPods and the car, and I'm not sure I can hear the difference on my gear anyway. Would be a different story if they added real hi-fi for the extra cost.

Still cheap for that library and for Discover Weekly. The repetitive recommendations and the hidden discovery playlists are annoying, but a small price bump doesn't change my mind. Still better than Apple Music's algorithm imo.
Sure, a small increase is fine since the catalog is absurdly cheap, but artists still get almost nothing per stream. Raise the price and then pay the artists better and I'll stop complaining.
Rolled my app back and turned off auto updates to keep the old version. Now they raise the price too? If the new layout gets forced on me again I'm done, the day I cancel is coming fast.
Student plan goes up a buck. Still the best deal with Hulu included, but I'm watching my budget more now since Showtime is gone. Not a fan of this one.
Another price bump and the app still has the same bugs since the last update. Support never fixed it. Can we get the thing working before we charge more?

UI changes burying my library and the AI DJ clutter, and now they want more money? YouTube Music has a great app and a great deal. I'm seriously looking at switching, the only thing keeping me is the recommendations.
Nickel and dime. Heart buttons are gone, I can't add the same song twice, and now they want more money for it. Money grubbing at its finest. I'd pay for the heart button back, but not like this.
Price is fine if the features are worth it. Spotlight is still my favorite discovery tool, and I'll keep putting in the setup effort. Still bummed they removed the repeat stuff though.
A dollar more is fine by me. I'm on it all day, collaborative playlists and Connect make it worth it. Would love lossless, but I can't see myself going back to anything else.
